page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv5 family, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores from an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The architecture incorporates 128.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and vector instruction extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI, along with hardware-accelerated AES and VAES cryptography. The configuration includes 1288 GB of local SSD storage and operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently within the middle 50% across general computing categories. It delivers a PassMark CPU score of 36,630.16 and a Geekbench multi-core result of 14,148.0, with a single-core score of 1,657.0. Large-block uncached memory operations register at 146.94 GB/sec for reads and 69.03 GB/sec for writes. The system handles 31.36 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 33.56 GB/sec. Decompression throughput reaches 152.59 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 benchmarks.

The absence of dedicated accelerator hardware results in expected performance degradation during large language model tasks, dropping to 2.29 tokens per second on 70B parameter models, though small 135M parameter models execute at a strong 287.54 tokens per second. With integrated local SSD capacity and balanced computational throughput, the server represents a balanced resource profile without requiring premium memory overhead. The instance fits transactional databases, in-memory caching systems, CI/CD software compilation, and mid-tier enterprise web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs, 128.0 GB of RAM with a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and 1288 GB of bundled local SSD storage, operating without GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations place the server within the median range for general computing, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 36,630.16 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 14,148.0. Uncached read memory bandwidth reaches 146.94 GB/sec, supporting 31.36 million Redis SET operations per second and 33.56 GB/sec in static web serving. While unsuited for large-scale AI inference due to missing accelerators, its integrated storage and balanced core density make it an effective platform for relational databases, distributed caching, enterprise web applications, and software build pipelines.
